title: Vega-Lite charts (.vl.json, .vl)
summary: A chart is laid out and drawn as one still picture; a defined subset of Vega-Lite 5 and 6.

items.text: Files: .vl.json and .vl, or a .json file whose top-level $schema is a Vega-Lite schema. A $schema of version 5 or 6 (version 6 defaults apply) or none.
Views: a single view, layer, concat, hconcat, vconcat, facet, and repeat.
Data: inline values, a relative local url (JSON, CSV, TSV, or DSV in the specification's folder and below), sequence, and the datasets of the specification.
Marks: bar, rect, point, circle, square, rule, tick, line, area, trail, text, arc, boxplot, errorbar, errorband.

Channels: x, y, xOffset, yOffset (grouped bars and offset points within a band or a time unit), theta, radius, color, fill, stroke, size, opacity, fillOpacity, strokeOpacity, strokeWidth, strokeDash, shape, angle, text, order, detail, and the secondary channels x2, y2, theta2, radius2, and the xError and yError channels of errorbar and errorband.
Field types quantitative, temporal, nominal, ordinal; aggregate, bin, timeUnit, stack, impute, sort, and condition.

A field without a type gets Vega-Lite's default, by the first rule that applies: quantitative on latitude and longitude; nominal on row, column, facet, shape, and strokeDash; ordinal on order or with a sort array; temporal with a timeUnit; quantitative with a bin or an aggregate other than argmin and argmax; quantitative for a numeric or discretizing scale.type, temporal for time or utc; and nominal otherwise - also on x and y. A datum takes its type from its value (a number is quantitative, a date-time object temporal, anything else nominal), and x2, y2, theta2, and radius2 take the type of their main channel. Write the type when another is meant.

Scales (linear, log, pow, sqrt, symlog, sequential, time, utc, band, point, ordinal, quantile, quantize, threshold, bin-ordinal), axes, legends, 68 named color schemes, titles, autosize, and container sizes. labelExpr of axes, legends, and facet headers (and config.axis and config.header) runs on datum.value and datum.label.
Transforms: calculate, filter, fold, flatten, sample, pivot, lookup, timeUnit, aggregate, joinaggregate, window, bin, stack, impute.

Selection params (select: point or interval, and the legacy selection of a view) in the state their value gives (none means empty): conditions with a param, a test that names one, and filters on one (the empty rule applies), and expressions that read the selection; the caller can replace the value of a param. A point selection projects over fields or encodings, an interval over encodings, and the tuples are matched as Vega does (an interval includes both ends). An interval selection with a value draws its brush as Vega-Lite does (a shade behind the marks and an outline in front, from select.mark and config.selection.interval.mark; one brush for a selection resolved globally, none in a facet); bind: scales sets the domain of the scales of a single view or of the layers of a top-level layered view (and is ignored in a concat, facet, or repeat); a selection can be the domain of a scale or the extent of a bin, in an encoding or in a bin transform.

A subset of the Vega expression language with 104 functions (including format, timeFormat and utcFormat, and the selection functions), static variable params (the expr of a param wins over its value), and expression references ({"expr": ...}) wherever Vega-Lite allows one and no row is involved: titles, padding, background, mark, axis, legend, header, scale, and view properties, and config. Each is evaluated once, with the params at their initial value. A scale domain can be an array of references or {"param": name} of a variable or selection param: the value of the param is then the domain as it is (no zero, nice, or padding) and the marks are clipped to the view; a bin extent of the form {"param": name} sets the span that chooses the bin width.

Dates in UTC; text drawn with the bundled Liberation fonts, and a character they lack (such as the math sign U+221D) taken from the bundled Noto Sans, Noto Sans Math, or Noto Sans Symbols 2, per character; a character none covers is drawn as the font's missing-glyph box and warned about (vl-text-missing-glyph).
Marks image and geoshape; geographic data, the longitude and latitude channels, projection, and the geojson field type.

Interaction: events, input widgets, and bindings are ignored (a selection is drawn in the state its value gives). The legend that a selection is bound to (bind "legend") dims the entries the selection does not hold to config.legend.unselectedOpacity (0.35), symbols and labels, as Vega-Lite does. Variable params inside a layer or a composition are ignored, as Vega-Lite itself declares no signal for them. A lookup from a param (the data of a selection) is reported and not applied.

A point selection without fields or encodings (it selects rows by identity) with an initial value, animation selections (a timer), and a top-level selection of a layered view with two or more layers (Vega rejects it): each is reported and applied as an empty selection.

An xOffset or yOffset without a nominal or ordinal position channel to nest in, or a temporal one with a time unit to nest in (not day or weekday, binned or maxbins; not a rect mark), and a quantitative or temporal offset of a bar or area (a ranged offset).
Transforms regression, loess, density, quantile, and extent.
legend.encode and axis.encode, and a custom formatType.
Expression functions outside the 104, signal, event, and item, and the bitwise and in operators.
Remote data: a url with a scheme, a drive letter, or an absolute path is never fetched; the chart is drawn with an empty dataset.
values given as text, custom SVG-path shapes, cubehelix interpolation, the identity scale, and scale properties such as bins.
Faceting by a binned, aggregated, or time-unit field, and facet sort by an aggregate.
Vega (as opposed to Vega-Lite) specifications.
Anything injected from the command line: there is no option for datasets, parameters, configuration, a data folder, a time zone, or fonts.
Multiply the laid-out size by a factor.
Fit the chart to a width, keeping its aspect ratio; --height does the same for the height.
Fit the chart inside a box and center it.
Replace the background the chart declares (white when it declares none); transparent keeps alpha.
Fail with unsupported-feature instead of leaving a construct out.
A chart has one page, so only 1 is valid; a larger number is page-out-of-range.
The model options (-D, --view, ...) are a usage-error for a chart. 'canvasnet info' reports the laid-out size, marks, and data references without drawing.

Identifiers have the form vl-<area>-<detail>, in lower case. An unsupported construct is listed in diagnostics[] as {source: vega-lite, severity: unsupported, code: <id>} (without --json, also as an 'Unsupported: <id>: <message>' line on standard error); the message gives file, line, column, and JSON pointer. With --strict the first one fails with unsupported-feature.
A mark that is not drawn, for example vl-mark-geoshape; the view is drawn without marks.
A longitude or latitude channel.
A url with a scheme, a drive letter, or an absolute path: never fetched, empty dataset.
Geographic data (sphere, graticule, topojson).
A projection.

A top-level selection param of a layered view that has two or more layers: Vega-Lite compiles duplicate signals that Vega rejects; the selection is applied as empty (declare it in one layer, or name the layer in views).
A point selection with no fields or encodings and an initial value: it selects rows by identity, which is not modeled; the selection is applied as empty.
An animation selection (on: timer): drawn in its initial state, without the animation.

Warning: a selection cannot be projected over a channel (the view has no field on it, or its field is aggregated), an interval selection is initialized with a key that is not a channel, a selection used as a scale domain or a bin extent names no usable field and projects several (the first is used), or a selection bound to the scales projects a channel without a continuous scale.
A variable param of a nested view (a layer or a composition): Vega-Lite declares no signal for it, so it is ignored and an expression that reads it sees null (Vega fails).
A lookup transform whose from is a param (the data of a selection): it needs the final table of another view filtered by the selection, which is not supported yet; the transform is not applied.
An {"expr": ...} where Vega-Lite's schema allows none (a width or height, for example), or in a place with no row that reads datum.
A transform that is not run, for example vl-transform-regression.
An expression function outside the supported 104, for example vl-expr-function-now: the call evaluates to null.
axis.encode or legend.encode.
An xOffset or yOffset that has no nominal or ordinal x or y channel (or a temporal one with a time unit that can hold it) to nest in: the offset is ignored.
A quantitative or temporal xOffset or yOffset of a bar or area (a ranged offset): the offset is ignored.
A custom SVG-path shape: a circle is drawn.
A scale type that is not supported, for example vl-scale-identity.
The geojson field type.
Warning: a property Vega-Lite does not define for that object.
Warning: a $schema that is not version 5 or 6; version 6 defaults are used.
Warning: autosize fit together with a step size; the fit is dropped for that dimension.
Warning: the value of a param used as a scale domain (or a domainRaw) is not an array of at least two numbers or dates (one value for a band, point, or ordinal scale); the scale keeps its own domain.
Warning: a width, height, padding, config, or similar property of a composition that only the top-level view decides.

Warning: text with characters that neither the font nor the bundled fallback fonts have a glyph for (for example a private-use or CJK character); the font's missing-glyph box is drawn. Reported at the text mark, or with no location for axis labels, legends, and titles.

Warnings have the code vega-lite-warning and carry the vl-* identifier at the start of the message text, after the location. Errors: vega-lite-error (invalid specification, a data file that is missing or refused, a chart that cannot be drawn), budget-exceeded (a library limit), corrupt-input (a specification longer than {{vlMaxSourceLength}} characters), and size-limit (a chart laid out beyond {{maxDimension}} pixels on a side).
See the Vega-Lite section of the Vega-Lite user guide for the complete list of identifiers.

The picture is static: no interaction, and tooltips are omitted. A selection or a param is drawn in its initial state, as vega-embed paints it before any event; a date in a selection value is read in UTC. The brush of an initial interval selection is drawn (nothing is made for a brush with no extent, where Vega-Lite makes a zero-size rectangle), and bind: scales applies where Vega-Lite applies it to a still chart.
A schema of version 5 is drawn with the version 6 defaults (a view is 300 by 300 pixels by default, for example).

Text is measured with the bundled fonts, so labels, legends, and facet headers can differ from a browser by a few pixels. A character the Liberation fonts lack is drawn from the bundled Noto fonts, never from an installed font, so the result does not depend on the machine.
Dates are always UTC; nothing is read from the network; data files are only read from the specification's folder and below.
A chart can be drawn inside an SVG diagram with <image href="chart.vl.json" .../> (see 'canvasnet help svg'); it keeps its own background there.
Color schemes are interpolated piecewise in sRGB, not taken from the d3-scale-chromatic tables.

labelExpr and the other expressions have format(value, specifier) (d3-format), timeFormat() and utcFormat() (d3-time-format); an invalid specifier is a render error. config.legend.labelExpr is not read, as in Vega-Lite 6.
Composite marks (boxplot, errorbar, errorband) report binned, aggregated, or time-unit grouping channels and do not apply them.
A shared legend shows the symbols of the first layer.
Compositions drop more properties than Vega-Lite does; each is reported as a warning.
Delimited text is not type-inferred (as in Vega): cells stay strings unless format.parse says otherwise.
A line feed inside title text splits the title into lines, which Vega itself does not do.
Compared with vega-embed: no actions menu, no signals, no renderer choice, and no config or datasets injection from the command line.
